meta.purpose: The decision-blocking register. Every question here is one that cannot be answered from the material available to this build. Each records what is already known, what is missing, what decision it blocks, and the cheapest way to find the missing answer.
meta.rule: No question below is answered by inference. Where the answer exists in a document, the question is marked answerable and the source is linked. Where it exists only in the owner's account, it is marked owner-only.

questions.question: Is shopnow047c-20 an approved Associates storefront, and is the account in good standing?
questions.known: The tag was supplied in the brief. S01 and S02 set out what an approved account is and what happens to links that are not properly tagged.
questions.missing: Whether the account exists, is approved, and is current. This is knowable only from inside the account.
questions.blocks: Every product link. No link should go live until this is answered.
questions.howToFind: Associates Central → Account Settings → confirm the storefront ID. If the account is not yet approved, apply first and leave the site's buy buttons in their current no-tag state.

questions.question: Are the five supplied link.amazon links compliant Special Links for this account?
questions.known: All five were opened once. None carried a visible tag parameter. All five resolved to an ASIN different from the code in the URL.
questions.missing: Whether link.amazon is an Amazon-sanctioned shortener for Associates links in the owner's region, and whether these five carry a hidden tag. Neither can be settled from the redirect alone.
questions.blocks: Replacing the placeholder links with live ones at scale.
questions.howToFind: Run the one-link enrollment test in link-audit.json. Generate one SiteStripe link, click it once, and confirm the click appears in the tracking report. If it does, generate the other four the same way.

questions.question: Where exactly does the disclosure have to sit to satisfy both Amazon and the FTC, and is once per page enough?
questions.known: S01 Section 5 names the sentence. S05 says a disclosure behind a click or at the end of a page is likely to be missed, and that disclosures must be hard to miss.
questions.missing: Nothing material. This is answerable from the two documents and has been implemented as a strip under the masthead plus a footer repeat on every page.
questions.blocks: Nothing — this one is settled.
questions.howToFind: Already resolved. See the compliance page for the resulting rule set.

questions.question: Can this site publish buying advice for products nobody here has handled?
questions.known: S05 forbids describing experience with a product you have not tried. It does not forbid publishing factual comparisons of documented specifications.
questions.missing: Whether the owner intends to fund physical testing, and whether the site should stay a listing-and-documentation desk or become a test lab.
questions.blocks: The entire editorial voice, and whether the site can ever claim first-hand experience.
questions.howToFind: A decision, not a lookup. Pick between Path A and Path B on the Suggestions page.

questions.question: Where does event data go, and who is allowed to receive it?
questions.known: The site records five defined events with no cookie and no identifier. A collection endpoint has to exist somewhere for that to be a measurement rather than a log line.
questions.missing: Whether the owner will host an endpoint, use a hosted analytics product, or stay with browser-local counts. Each has a different disclosure obligation under S02 Participation Requirements 3(e).
questions.blocks: Any statement about traffic or clicks, and the choice of next article.
questions.howToFind: Choose one of the three on the Metrics page. The page documents what each choice obliges you to disclose.

questions.question: Is the product set meant to be five air-fryer-cooking items, or is a thermometer a misfit?
questions.known: Three air fryers and two thermometers. Both thermometers list air fryer among their uses. That is a defensible editorial spine: fryer plus the tool that tells you when the food is done.
questions.missing: Whether the owner intends to add more thermometers (making a category) or more fryers (making a single-category site with an accessory shelf).
questions.blocks: Site taxonomy and where the next ten products go.
questions.howToFind: Owner decision. The site currently ships the two-category structure, which works either way.

questions.question: Is The Crisp Kitchen a name the owner wants to keep, and is it clear of Amazon marks?
questions.known: S02 Participation Requirements 1(g) and Trademark Guidelines 8 forbid Amazon marks or confusingly similar names in a domain, subdomain, tag, username or app name.
questions.missing: Whether the owner will register a domain, and whether a trademark search has been run on the working name.
questions.blocks: Domain registration, social handles, and the final masthead.
questions.howToFind: Run a USPTO word-mark search on the chosen name and a domain availability check. Neither was done here, because the build must not imply a legal clearance it did not perform.

questions.question: Which four guide topics should exist first, and on what basis?
questions.known: Four question-shaped working titles were proposed in the brief. All four are published. None is supported by search-volume data, and the site says so on every guide.
questions.missing: Actual query demand. Guessing it is how sites end up publishing into silence.
questions.blocks: The publishing cadence and the next topic.
questions.howToFind: Turn on measurement first (Q-05). After 30 days, sort the five events by source and pick the topic the data points at, not the topic that sounds good.

questions.question: Is there budget or intent to test any product physically?
questions.known: Nothing here was tested. Every claim on the site is labelled as either a listing claim or an editorial inference.
questions.missing: Budget, and willingness to buy a unit that may not sell.
questions.blocks: Whether the site can rank on judgement instead of on restated specifications.
questions.howToFind: Owner decision. Cheapest credible start: buy the two thermometers, which cost the least to test objectively (ice bath, boiling water, a timed oven ramp).

questions.question: Should the site stay on GitHub Pages, or move to a host that can run a collection endpoint?
questions.known: GitHub Pages serves static files and cannot accept a POST from the outbound-click counter.
questions.missing: Whether the owner has another host, a serverless account, or a preference for a hosted analytics product.
questions.blocks: Q-05 and the whole measurement plan.
questions.howToFind: Any free serverless function endpoint will do. The client already posts one small JSON body to a configurable URL.

questions.question: Is the repository intended to be public, and should the data files be public with it?
questions.known: The repository is public and GitHub Pages already serves from main.
questions.missing: Whether the owner is comfortable publishing the full source register, including the unresolved flags.
questions.blocks: Nothing technically. It is a policy choice.
questions.howToFind: Owner decision. The current build assumes transparency is the point, and publishes the flags deliberately.

questions.question: Does the privacy page need to name every third party that sets anything?
questions.known: S02 Participation Requirements 3(e) requires accurate disclosure of cookies, pixels and third-party technologies, through a privacy policy or otherwise.
questions.missing: The final list of third parties, which depends on Q-05 and Q-10. As built, the site sets no cookies and loads no third-party script.
questions.blocks: The accuracy of the privacy page once analytics is switched on.
questions.howToFind: Re-read the privacy page the day analytics is enabled. It currently states the zero-third-party position, which is true today and will stop being true the moment an analytics product is added.

questions.question: Should the site show prices at all, and if so, how?
questions.known: S02 permits price display only when Amazon serves it or when it comes from Creators API / PA API with a timestamp and the required disclaimer. Static prices copied by hand satisfy neither route.
questions.missing: Whether the owner has or will request Creators API access, or is willing to use SiteStripe widgets.
questions.blocks: Any price comparison feature, and any article whose value depends on price.
questions.howToFind: Apply for Creators API access inside Associates Central, or use SiteStripe native widgets, which serve the data themselves.

questions.question: How often should the product table be re-checked, and by what mechanism?
questions.known: Listings change. Every row carries an observed date of 2026-11-20.
questions.missing: Whether to automate the re-check. Automation is constrained: S02 forbids data-mining and robots, and the Agent Terms require any agent to identify itself in the user agent string.
questions.blocks: Whether the table can be trusted after a month.
questions.howToFind: Either re-check manually monthly, or obtain API access and let the API serve the data. Crawling is not an option.
questions.effort: 20 minutes per month, or API access

questions.question: What happens to the site if the account is terminated?
questions.known: S01 Section 6 allows termination on written notice with a 7-day effective date, and treats a Section 5 violation as a material breach.
questions.missing: An operational plan. If the account ends, every tagged link and every display of Amazon content must stop.
questions.blocks: Nothing now. It is the failure plan.
questions.howToFind: Documented on the Compliance page as a one-step kill switch: the site has a single link-configuration point, so removing the tag and the Amazon-derived content is one file change.

questions.question: Who is the named author, and is a pen name acceptable?
questions.known: The site currently publishes under an editorial-desk byline, not a person's name.
questions.missing: Whether the owner wants a named human author, which affects trust signals and is a decision only the owner can make.
questions.blocks: Author pages, structured data, and any future E-E-A-T signalling.
questions.howToFind: Owner decision. Do not invent a person; a desk byline is honest until a real person is willing to be named.

questions.question: Should each product have its own page, or is a category grid enough?
questions.known: Category grids plus comparison tables are live. Individual product URLs do not exist yet.
questions.missing: Whether one page per product adds enough unique information to be worth indexing, or whether it would be thin content behind five near-identical templates.
questions.blocks: Whether to add /products/<slug>.html × 5.
questions.howToFind: Publish the five as noindex-free pages only once each has at least one thing the grid does not: a measured dimension, a tested result, or a documented trade-off. Until then, the grid is the better page.

questions.question: What is the business entity, and does it need a contact address on the site?
questions.known: The site publishes no address and no legal entity.
questions.missing: The entity name and a contactable address. Depending on jurisdiction, a trading site may need both.
questions.blocks: Terms of use and any serious commercial trust signal.
questions.howToFind: Owner decision plus local advice. This build does not give legal advice and says so.

questions.question: Do the two certification claims (NIST, NSF) survive a registry check?
questions.known: Both appear in seller listing text and are reproduced only as seller claims.
questions.missing: Whether the models appear in the certifying bodies' public records.
questions.blocks: Any ranking of those two products on accuracy, and any article that repeats the claim.
questions.howToFind: Search the NSF product and service listings for the model, and NIST's calibration records. Record certificate numbers if found; record absence if not.

questions.question: Is the five-product set stable enough to design around?
questions.known: Five ASINs are recorded with an observation date. ASINs may be stored indefinitely under S02 IP License 2(h); the listing content attached to them may not be cached.
questions.missing: Whether any of the five is being discontinued. A dead ASIN on a live page is a broken recommendation.
questions.blocks: Whether to build comparison pages that depend on all five.
questions.howToFind: Check for the availability statement on each page monthly, and re-check before any campaign that spends money.
